title: Natural genus-exclusive four-position VP24 configuration in Bundibugyo virus links host interferon tone to a testable cell-type ordering
abstract: Abstract Bundibugyo virus (BDBV) causes outbreaks with lower case-fatality than Ebola virus (EBOV); its VP24 carries the only BDBV-specific functional difference mapped to date. That difference was defined in an engineered virus. Here, we integrate a sequence census, a human cell-type expression atlas, and a reanalysis of public infection data to connect the natural BDBV VP24 configuration to host interferon (IFN) tone and derive a testable cell-type ordering of post-entry IFN-mediated restriction. All 31 full-length BDBV VP24 records and all 36 complete 2026 outbreak genomes carried S83/Q135/H140/A141; none of the other five orthoebolavirus species assessed carried the complete set. Two consensus-only single-position departures occurred among 860 callable copies in the surveillance data. Δ, a baseline IFN-tone score, tracks the IFN-stimulated level attained by a cell and predicts the strength of IFN-mediated suppression of viral RNA accumulation in cells infected with BDBV carrying the VP24 defect: high Δ denotes stronger suppression, low Δ weaker. Across 154 human cell types, Δ was higher in surface epithelia and circulating myeloid cells (enterocytes 1.28; monocytes 1.00) than in retinal and testicular cells (retinal pigment epithelium − 1.02; Sertoli cells − 0.68). A competing importin-α model predicted exemption in the 47 cell types with high Δ but low importin-α, including enteric epithelium and hepatocytes. In the HIV-1 restriction panel, Δ discriminated restricted from permissive cells (area under the curve (AUC) 0.87), whereas importin-α was at chance (AUC 0.47–0.50); functional data therefore descriptively support Δ.

title: Marked Geographic Heterogeneity in Ebola Virus Disease Case Fatality During the 17th Outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, 2026: a Health Zone Level Funnel Plot Analysis
abstract: Abstract Background The Ebola case fatality ratio (CFR) classically varies by geographic and operational context, but this heterogeneity has rarely been formally quantified sub-nationally in real time during an active outbreak. Methods From 142 situation reports (SitReps) (May 18 to October 3, 2026), we extracted confirmed cases/deaths for 64 health zones, calculated CFR with 95% Wilson confidence intervals, tested heterogeneity by chi-square, and visualised it by Spiegelhalter funnel plot, excluding a block of 493 unallocated Ituri deaths from zone/province analyses ; sensitivity analyses tested four alternative ways of handling these deaths. Results Zone-summed CFR ranged from 33.3% (South Kivu) to 58.5% (North Kivu, 95% CI 56.1–60.8), via 38.3% in Ituri (95% CI 37.1–39.5); heterogeneity was highly significant (x 2 = 227.1, df = 6, p 2 = 193.5, df = 12, p Case fatality shows robust, persisting geographic heterogeneity at two scales, with a real but limited inter-provincial convergence since September, warranting targeted investigation of treatment-capacity and care-seeking determinants.

title: Quantifying the extinction probability of Marburg virus disease outbreaks: A continuous-time Markov chain model integrating a multi-type branching process
abstract: Understanding the extinction dynamics of Marburg virus disease is crucial, particularly during the early stages of an outbreak when stochastic effects strongly influence disease outcomes. Although deterministic models have provided valuable insights into virus transmission dynamics, they cannot adequately capture random transmission events or quantify extinction probabilities, particularly when outbreaks begin with few infected cases. This study develops a continuous-time Markov chain stochastic model derived from a deterministic multi-host transmission model. The model incorporates a multi-type branching process, in which distinct infectious types are tracked according to their contributions to secondary infections, enabling estimation of disease extinction probabilities during the early outbreak phase. The extinction analysis shows that outbreaks initiated by exposed humans have a higher probability of extinction (21.6%) compared with those initiated by infectious humans (13.7%), whereas outbreaks initiated by infected bats have an extinction probability of only 0.36%, highlighting their role as important reservoirs sustaining virus transmission. Furthermore, the results demonstrate that reducing human-to-human transmission, decreasing viral shedding, and increasing environmental viral decay significantly enhance the likelihood of disease extinction. The proposed framework provides a quantitative tool for assessing Marburg virus disease outbreak risk and valuable insights for designing early interventions for human transmission, environmental contamination, and cross-species interactions.

title_zh: 量化马尔堡病毒病 暴发的灭绝概率:一种整合多类型分支过程的连续时间马尔可夫链模型
source_body_en: Understanding the extinction dynamics of Marburg virus disease is crucial, particularly during the early stages of an outbreak when stochastic effects strongly influence disease outcomes. Although deterministic models have provided valuable insights into virus transmission dynamics, they cannot adequately capture random transmission events or quantify extinction probabilities, particularly when outbreaks begin with few infected cases. This study develops a continuous-time Markov chain stochastic model derived from a deterministic multi-host transmission model. The model incorporates a multi-type branching process, in which distinct infectious types are tracked according to their contributions to secondary infections, enabling estimation of disease extinction probabilities during the early outbreak phase. The extinction analysis shows that outbreaks initiated by exposed humans have a higher probability of extinction (21.6%) compared with those initiated by infectious humans (13.7%), whereas outbreaks initiated by infected bats have an extinction probability of only 0.36%, highlighting their role as important reservoirs sustaining virus transmission. abstract_zh: 理解马尔堡病毒病的灭绝动力学至关重要,尤其是在暴发初期阶段,随机效应对疾病结果有显著影响。尽管确定性模型为病毒传播动力学提供了有价值的见解,但它们无法充分捕捉随机传播事件或量化灭绝概率,特别是在暴发初始病例较少时。本研究基于一个确定性多宿主 传播模型,开发了一个连续时间马尔可夫链随机模型。该模型采用多类型分支过程,根据不同感染类型对二次感染的贡献进行追踪,从而能够在暴发初期阶段估计疾病灭绝概率。灭绝分析表明,由暴露人类引发的暴发灭绝概率为21.6%,高于由传染性人类引发的暴发(13.7%),而由感染蝙蝠引发的暴发灭绝概率仅为0.36%,突显了蝙蝠作为重要储存宿主维持病毒传播的作用。此外,研究结果表明,减少人传人传播、降低病毒排毒量以及增加环境病毒衰减显著提高了疾病灭绝的可能性。所提出的框架为评估马尔堡病毒病 暴发风险提供了定量工具,并为设计针对人类传播、环境污染和跨物种互动的早期干预措施提供了有价值的见解。

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 理解马尔堡病毒病的灭绝动力学至关重要,尤其是在暴发的早期阶段,随机效应对疾病结果有显著影响。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 本研究基于一个确定性多宿主 传播模型,开发了一个连续时间马尔可夫链随机模型。
analysis_zh.methods: 该模型采用多类型分支过程,根据不同感染类型对二次感染的贡献进行追踪,从而能够在暴发初期阶段估计疾病灭绝概率。

analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 结果表明,减少人与人之间的传播传播、降低病毒排毒量以及增加环境中的病毒降解率,会显著提高疾病灭绝的可能性。
